question: to the Commission Dario Tamburrano (The Left) Subject:
The Salone biodigester has, since the submission of question for written answer E002339/20261, been granted NRRP funding.2 I ask the Commission the following: 1.

In the light of the facts outlined in question E-002339/2026 and given that the Salone plan calls for the sealing of four hectares of fertile farmland, could the Commission clarify whether this project has undergone a DNSH assessment and whether Italy will be held to account if it fails to fulfil its obligations in this regard?

Given that the proposers behind the Salone project suggested making several major changes3 during the environmental impact assessment phase, that the cumulative impact of the planned facility and of the area’s other large waste installations4 was not assessed, and that no attempt seems to have been made to estimate the future plant’s total gas levels – which are necessary to establish whether the Salone biodigester should be subject to the provisions laid down by Directive 2012/18/EU – can the Commission say whether Italy has, in this specific case, correctly applied the relevant EU legislation? What measures will the Commission take if it transpires that Italy’s handling of this matter is at odds with European law?

Does the Commission agree that the facts outlined in Complaint No CPLT(2026)01422 show that the recent raft of authorised waste treatment plants in and around Rome are evidence that Italy is systematically violating EU law?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.9.2026) Compliance with the Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) principle is a prerequisite for a measure to be included in a recovery and resilience plan (RRP). The Commission assessed compliance of the Italian RRP with the DNSH principle ex ante, at investment level1. The Council Implementing Decision2 on the updated RRP for Italy requires projects financed under ‘Investment 1.4 - Development of biomethane, according to criteria for promoting the circular economy’ to comply with the DNSH principle3. National authorities must ensure compliance with DNSH requirements during the implementation of the individual projects. They are competent to assess claims of potential environmental harm caused by specific projects. Where a project was authorised after an assessment in accordance with Directive 2011/92/EU4 and the state of the environment changed afterwards, or where new findings regarding the impact of the project on the environment emerge between the time the project was authorised and its actual execution, the assessment may need to be updated or extended, taking into account the legitimate expectations of the public and the principle of good administration. Moreover, biogas may be classified under the Seveso III Directive5 as a flammable gas6 or a liquified flammable gas7 with thresholds applicable to lower-tier and upper-tier establishments8. Establishments where those gases are or may be present in quantities exceeding those thresholds fall under the scope of the Directive. It is for the national authorities to assess whether this is the case or not and to ensure compliance of individual projects with EU legislation9. Complaint CPLT(2026)01422 is pending and handled in accordance with the complaint handling procedure. 1 In accordance with the criteria laid down in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2021/241 of the European

Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2021 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility, OJ L 57, 18.2.2021. 2 https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-12357-2026-ADD-1/en/pdf. 3 As set out in the DNSH Technical Guidance (2021/C58/01). 4 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (codification), OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, as amended. 5 Directive 2012/18/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 July 2012 on the control of majoraccident hazards involving dangerous substances, amending and subsequently repealing Council Directive 96/82/EC, OJ L 197, 24.7.2012. 6 Entry P2 of part 1 of Annex I to the Seveso III Directive. 7 Pursuant to note 19 of Annex I of the Seveso III Directive, for the purpose of the implementation of the Directive, upgraded biogas may be classified under entry 18 of Part 2 of Annex I where it has been processed in accordance with applicable standards for purified and upgraded biogas ensuring a quality equivalent to that of natural gas, including the content of Methane, and which has a maximum of 1 % Oxygen. 8 Stricter legal requirements apply to installations handling high amounts: upper tier establishments, as opposed to lower tier establishments, with lower quantities of dangerous substances and hence presenting a lower risk. 9 Commission Communication "EU law: Better results through better application (C/2016/8600), OJ C 18, 19.1.2017. This approach was confirmed by the Communication entitled EU law for a Europe that delivers (COM(2022)518).
